headline: Granted extension, special permits, and variances for six zoning applications; continued two others.
summary: The Zoning Board of Appeals heard several requests for variances and special permits on properties across the city and granted relief in most cases after public comment. The board also continued two applications to the April 22, 2026 meeting and approved prior meeting minutes.
decisions: Granted a 6-month extension of the variance for Stilt House-Atlantic Overlook LLC at 68 Paine Avenue to October 23, 2026, vote 5-0.
Granted a Special Permit for Julie Sorkin at 28 Ashton Street to construct a basement, first floor and deck addition, subject to plans submitted, vote 5-0.
Granted a Special Permit for Alan Synenki at 13 Butterworth Road to construct a building addition with the setback and expansion relief requested, subject to plans submitted, vote 5-0.
Granted a Special Permit for Guy Bouchard at 32 Pratt Avenue to construct a shed dormer, subject to plans submitted, vote 5-0.
Granted a Variance for David Veritas at 6 Greenleaf Drive to construct a detached 2-car garage and ADU in the front yard, subject to plans submitted, vote 5-0.
Granted a continuance for Albert Turner's application at 26 Mason Street to the April 22, 2026 meeting, subject to signing the Waiver and Agreement, vote 5-0.
Granted a Variance for Paul Clermont at 8 Upland Road to construct a two-car open-air carport with 7.2 ft of relief, subject to gutter conditions and plans submitted, vote 5-0.
Granted a continuance for Jason Irving/21 Bridge Street LLC's application at 21 Bridge Street to the April 22, 2026 meeting, subject to signing the Waiver and Agreement, vote 5-0.
Approved the February 25, 2026 meeting minutes as written, vote 5-0.
plain_text:
CITY of BEVERLY 
Zoning Board of Appeals 
March 25, 2026 at 7:00 pm 
  
These minutes are not a verbatim transcript of the public hearing of the Board of Appeals.  
Reviews of these Minutes or outcome of the public hearing should include an examination of the 
Board’s decision for that hearing.   
 
 
Members Present:  Will Cosmas, Chairperson, Michael Barone, Cory Farinella, Laura  
   Meisenhelter and Benjamin Roy 
 
Others Present:      Jim Butler, Building Commissioner 
Leanna Harris, Administrative Assistant 
 
Location:        Council Chambers City Hall, 191 Cabot Street, Beverly 
  
 
Will Cosmas began the meeting at 7:03pm and introduced the Board members present. 
 
EXTENSION REQUEST 
 
Glovsky & Glovsky o/b/o Stilt House-Atlantic Overlook LLC 
requests a Finding and Variances to authorize the construction of a single-family house and 
elevated driveway where the existing home will be partially demolished and converted to an 
accessory beach cabana, requiring the following relief: (1) variances from the 20-foot side 
setback required under Section 300-30(D)(4) to allow a 10.5’ side setback for the main residence, 
a minimum 14’ side setback for the pile supported driveway court and a 0’ side setback for the 
pile supported driveway ramp; (2) a variance from the 15’ maximum height allowed under 
Section 300-27E(2) for an accessory structure to allow the converted cabana to be maintained at 
its current height of approximately 20’ and (3) such relief that may be necessary to authorize the 
proposed project.  The property is located at 68 Paine Avenue in the R90 zoning district. 
 
Conor Walsh, Esq. (Glovsky & Glovsky) addressed the Board on behalf of the applicant and 
stated they were here in April of last year for the underlying application and the Board granted 
the relief requested. This project is a unique waterfront property, and the prior application 
involved the Conservation Commission and DEP due to its proximity to the ocean.  Atty. Walsh 
stated that last few months have been spent working towards approval but the applicant isn’t 
ready to pull building permit.  The applicant is requesting a 1-year continuance although a 6-
month extension is normal and agreed that the allowed duration under G.L. c. 40A, § 10 is 6 
months. 
 
Ms. Meisenhelter stated that it appears to her that an extension request can be up to 1-year. 
 
No one from the public spoke for or against.
Page 2 of 10 
MOTION:  Mr. Farinella moved to close the public hearing. 
Mr. Roy seconded the motion. 
V otes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy) 
Motion carries. 
 
Mr. Cosmas stated he would prefer to grant a 6-month extension in accordance with G.L. c. 40A, 
§10, which limits such extensions to a period not to exceed 6 months. 
 
MOTION:  Mr. Cosmas moved to GRANT the request to extend the Variance in 
accordance with Ch. 40A, Section 10 for 6-months to October 23, 2026.   
Mr. Barone seconded the Motion.   
V otes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy) 
Motion carries. 
 
 
NEW PUBLIC HEARING 
 
Julie Sorkin 
requests a Special Permit pursuant to Section 300-83A.2 of the Beverly Zoning Ordinance to 
construct a basement, first floor and deck addition on the rear of the existing single family 
dwelling requiring relief for encroachment into the right side yard setback. The property is 
located at 28 Ashton Street in the R10 zoning district.   
 
Jeff Tucker (Tucker Architecture) addressed the Board and stated the houses along this very 
narrow street are similar to cottages. According to Mr. Tucker, the home is a low 1½ story 
bungalow, and there is an existing garage that the applicant would like to keep. The existing 
dwelling is 8.1’ from the side lot line, the new addition is to the rear of the house and will line up 
with the existing house. Mr. Tucker stated that the addition will not encroach more into the 
setbacks and will not be visible from the road.   Mr. Tucker stated that due to the narrowness of 
the lot this is the only option for expansion.   
 
Mr. Barone asked if the existing deck on the right side of the house is being removed and Mr. 
Tucker confirmed.  Mr. Tucker stated they will be reducing the side impact on that side. 
 
No one from the public spoke for or against. 
 
Mr. Sorkin stated a few neighbors came by and inquired about the project.   
 
Mr. Cosmas asked what their lot backs up to and Mr. Sorkin stated it is a flood zone. 
 
Mr. Tucker stated it is a flat roofed addition with a walk out basement.  There is a full basement 
below that they will step down to create more head space and make the space more viable.  The 
new addition will make the house a 3-bedroom home.
Page 3 of 10 
MOTION: Mr. Barone moved to close the public hearing.   
Mr. Roy seconded the Motion. 
V otes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy) 
Motion carries. 
 
Mr. Farinella asked the applicant which neighbors were consulted about the project, and the 
applicant stated the project was discussed with the abutter to their right. 
 
Mr. Barone stated he thinks this is a fair request that it is a really good use of space on a narrow 
lot.  Mr. Barone stated that this part of Ryal Side is tight and he doesn’t think they are creating 
any issues. 
 
Mr. Roy stated he is impressed with the amount of living space they are gaining with such 
minimal impact.  Mr. Cosmas agreed and stated it is a very thoughtful plan. 
 
MOTION: Mr. Barone moved to GRANT a Special Permit at 28 Ashton Street pursuant 
to Section 300-83A.2 of the Beverly Zoning Ordinance to construct a basement, first 
floor and deck addition on the rear of the existing single family dwelling requiring relief 
for encroachment into the right side yard setback, subject to the plans submitted.  
Mr. Farinella seconded the Motion.  
V otes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy) 
Motion carries. 
 
Alan Synenki 
requests a Special Permit to construct a building addition with a front yard setback of 12.7' 
where 14.8' exists and 20.0' is required [§300-83A(2)].  Also, in accordance with §300-
83A(1)(b), the building footprint, gross floor area, and volume will be expanded by more than 
25% (50%, 29% and 33%, respectively).  The property is located at 13 Butterworth Road in the 
R10 zoning district.   
 
Bob Griffin (Griffin Engineering) addressed the Board and stated the applicants are both present.  
According to Mr. Griffin, the applicant seeks to move to this property in North Beverly because 
the applicant believe that it is a perfect spot to age in place. It is a nonconforming lot and 
building.  It is an 18,000 sq. ft. lot with about 90’ of frontage where 100’ is required.  The 
building is nonconforming because it doesn’t comply with the front or side yard setbacks.   
 
The proposal is to add a small front porch to create a place for the applicants to get into the house 
out of the weather.  Mr. Griffin reviewed the plans and elevations.  There is a 16’x 20’ deck in 
the backyard.  There will be a 1-car garage.  It is currently 14.8’ and will be reduced to12.7’.  
The applicants do not propose to increase the height of the building. 
 
A petition was submitted with abutters who have signed in favor.
Page 4 of 10 
Mr. Barone asked for clarification that the front porch currently exists and the proposal is to 
cover that porch.  Mr. Griffin confirmed and stated there is an uncovered entrance.  The porch is 
not being enclosed, the request for relief is for the roof. 
 
MOTION: Mr. Barone moved to close the public hearing.   
Mr. Roy seconded the Motion. 
V otes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy) 
Motion carries. 
 
MOTION: Mr. Roy moved to GRANT a Special Permit at 13 Butterworth Road to 
construct a building addition with a front yard setback of 12.7' where 14.8' exists and 
20.0' is required [§300-83A(2)].  Also, in accordance with §300-83A(1)(b), the building 
footprint, gross floor area, and volume will be expanded by more than 25% (50%, 29% 
and 33%, respectively), the building footprint and overall volume will be expanded more 
than 25% subject to the plans submitted.  Mr. Barone seconded the Motion.   
V otes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy) 
Motion carries. 
 
Glovsky & Glovsky o/b/o Guy Bouchard 
requests a Special Permit, and, in the alternative as to the right side of the house, a Variance, to 
allow for the construction a shed dormer to the back half of their legally nonconforming house to 
add a bathroom and enlarge the livable bedroom space on the second floor to accommodate the 
homeowner’s future needs. The addition will be no closer to any lot line than the existing 
structure, which is nonconforming as it relates to both side setbacks. The property is located at 
32 Pratt Avenue in the R10 zoning district. 
 
Correction:  The applicant is “Guy Bouchard” not “Gary Bouchard” as advertised. 
 
Conor Walsh, Esq. (Glovsky & Glovsky) addressed the Board on behalf of the applicant and 
stated they are seeking to construct a shed dormer on the rear of the dwelling, which they claim 
will allow for more viable space and the construction of a second-floor bathroom.  According to 
Atty. Walsh, the applicant’s lot is narrow and it is nonconforming with both rear and front 
setbacks.  The applicant has been considering this project for some time.  There is only one 
bathroom on the first floor, and recently, a tree fell and left the second floor uninhabitable.   
 
Atty. Walsh provided to the Board a map of the abutters who have signed off on the project.  
 
Steve Kranish, 30 Pratt Avenue, stated he was before this Board decades ago to discuss a similar 
project for his own property. The homes are both on modest lots with the same issues relating to 
setbacks. Mr. Kranish stated he went through this process to have the same shed dormer 
permitted and constructed on his house.  Mr. Kranish stated he thinks it’s a good addition to the 
home and is keeping with the neighborhood.  He sees nothing to object to.  
 
MOTION:  Mr. Roy moved to close the public hearing.   
Ms. Meisenhelter seconded the Motion.
Page 5 of 10 
V otes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy) 
Motion carries. 
 
Mr. Barone stated he thinks this is a fair request and he thinks a Special Permit under 83A(1)(b) 
would be sufficient relief for this request. Mr. Barone doesn’t think a Variance is needed.  
 
Ms. Meisenhelter stated the houses are in such close proximity that she is questioning where the 
construction equipment will go. 
 
Mr. Cosmas stated he agrees that the applicant only needs a Special Permit because the footprint 
isn’t changing. 
 
MOTION: Mr. Farinella moved to GRANT a Special Permit at 32 Pratt Avenue to allow 
for the construction a shed dormer to the back half of their legally nonconforming house 
to add a bathroom and enlarge the livable bedroom space on the second floor to 
accommodate the homeowner’s future needs. The addition will be no closer to any lot 
line than the existing structure, which is nonconforming as it relates to both side setbacks, 
subject to the plans submitted. Mr. Roy seconded the Motion. 
V otes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy) 
Motion carries. 
 
David Veritas 
requests a Variance to construct a single detached accessory structure that consists of a 2-car 
garage and accessory dwelling unit (ADU) in front of the existing single-family home. The 
variance will be from section 300-27B(2) of the zoning ordinance. The proposed accessory 
structure will meet all setbacks and height requirements. The property is located at 6 Greenleaf 
Drive in the R15 Zoning District. 
 
Brian Stein (Vance Stein Architects) stated that the applicant seeks a Variance for a new 
accessory dwelling unit (ADU) and a garage in the property’s front yard. According to Mr. Stein, 
the applicant has an elderly parent with mobility issues, the ADU will be accessible.  Mr. Stein 
stated that the lot is oddly shaped and it drops off significantly in the back, and the applicant 
requests to construct the ADU in the front yard due to the grade.  According to Mr. Stein, the lot 
is also fairly steep in the front; it is about 17’ feet above street level with a lot of trees. Mr. Stein 
stated that the area is very wooded and the ADU would not be visible to their neighbors or from 
the street, and applicant would face a significant cost increase to connect the ADU to the house 
 
Mr. Barone asked if the home has an existing garage and Mr. Stein stated there isn’t, there is a 
small shed. 
 
No one from the public spoke in favor or against.
Page 6 of 10 
MOTION: Mr. Farinella moved to close the public hearing. 
Mr. Barone seconded the motion. 
V otes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy) 
Motion carries. 
 
Mr. Cosmas asked if the applicant could build the proposed structure by right if it was connected 
in some way. Mr. Butler confirmed and stated if it connected to the house, they could build it by 
right.  The architect, Mr. Stein, stated it would look odd to connect the structures. 
 
Mr. Barone stated given the number of windows on the front of the house he can appreciate not 
wanting to adjoin to the front of the house.  Mr. Barone stated given the size of the lot and the 
wooded area it will be no less visible to the street than the existing house and he is not opposed 
to it.  It is a well thought out plan. 
 
MOTION: Mr. Farinella moved to GRANT a Variance at 6 Greenleaf Drive to construct 
a single detached accessory structure that consists of a 2-car garage and accessory 
dwelling unit (ADU) in front of the existing single-family home. The variance will be 
from section 300-27B(2) of the zoning ordinance. The proposed accessory structure will 
meet all setbacks and height requirements, subject to the plans submitted on the basis of 
the special conditions of the land and the shape of the lot.   Mr. Roy seconded the Motion. 
V otes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy) 
Motion carries. 
 
Albert Turner 
requests a Variance to construct a new detached single-car garage with an Accessory Dwelling 
Unit (ADU) above, in accordance with Sections 300-36 D(6) and D(8) of the Beverly Zoning 
Ordinance.  The property is located at 26 Mason Street in the RMD zoning district.   
 
Bill Nolan (Nolan Savoie) addressed the Board on behalf of the applicant and stated it is a  
4,000 sq. ft. lot containing a 3-story home.  According to Mr. Nolan, in the rear of the home is a 
foundation wall and concrete slab that they believe was for a garage. The applicant, Mr. Turner, 
bought this property in its current state, and they do not know when the garage was removed. 
The applicant is looking to reconstruct that garage with a small ADU studio apartment (285’) 
above.  The existing rear setback is 0.8’ where 20’ is required.   
 
The applicant would like to make the new garage narrower and move it forward a bit to 
accommodate the egress staircase from the ADU unit.  The idea was to connect the second story 
balcony with the new egress stairway but that would likely cause issues with sprinkling. Mr. 
Nolan stated that it is likely it will just be a solo staircase leading from the ADU down to grade.  
The applicant is considering creating an internal staircase down through the garage and believes 
that if they use a sprinkler system they can have one egress.  
 
The applicant would like to renovate the existing house and stay in the ADU.
Page 7 of 10 
Mr. Nolan stated that the hardship is that the existing topography in the rear is a full story up and 
also in the back of the property is a retaining wall for the property behind it. Due to the site-
specific conditions, the garage would need to be in the same location. 
 
Ms. Meisenhelter asked if the applicant received any feedback from neighbors.  Mr. Nolan stated 
the applicant did speak to the neighbors, but they did not receive any letters in support. 
 
Lauren Stafford, 25 Lyman Street stated she lives directly behind this property and if there are 
any windows in the back of the ADU he will be able to see directly into their backyard.  The 
houses are very close together.  Ms. Stafford stated she is fine with him building a garage she is 
not ok with an apartment above it because she believes it would affect their privacy. 
 
Mr. Nolan stated there aren’t many windows in the rear.  There is a small window above the 
kitchen sink that they could remove if it is a concern.   
 
Dana Marfongelli, Lyman Street stated he won’t be affected too much by it, but he is concerned 
that they will be setting a precedent.  Mr. Cosmas stated nothing this Board does sets a precedent. 
 
Gloria Pobiedzinski, 29 Lyman Street stated visually this doesn’t affect her but stated that she is 
concerned that this now makes the property a 4-family dwelling and the neighborhood is already 
so crowded.  She is concerned that some day they could turn the garage into a house. Ms. 
Pobiedzinski stated she doesn’t have a problem if it is just the garage.  
 
Brennan Postich, 205 Cabot Street, Apt. 10 stated this is the type of use that he needs to be able 
to live inside this City.  Mr. Postich stated ADUs are allowed by right and this would allow the 
applicant to save significant cost.   
 
Mr. Cosmas read the email received from Thomas Brennan opposing the proposal into record. 
 
Mr. Roy stated it’s a tight lot that will have 80% coverage.  
 
Mr. Cosmas stated he is concerned that there was no outreach to the rear abutter who is most 
affected by these plans.  Mr. Cosmas stated the applicant could request a continuance and use the 
time to reach out to abutters to alleviate concerns.  
 
Ms. Meisenhelter stated she is in favor of ADUs, but she thinks there are concerns that need to be 
addressed.  
 
Mr. Barone stated his biggest concerns are the additional cars, the density and the double height 
of the structure.  Mr. Nolan stated they are below the 35’ height restriction. 
 
Mr. Nolan stated he would like to request a continuance to the April meeting.  
 
MOTION: Mr. Barone moved GRANT a continuance to the April 22, 2026 meeting, 
subject to signing the Waiver and Agreement.  Mr. Roy seconded the motion.
Page 8 of 10 
V otes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy) 
Motion carries. 
 
Paul Clermont 
requests a Variance to construct a two-car open-air carport within the required 20 ft. front yard 
setback, seeking 7.2 ft. of relief per section 300-34-D3.  The property is located at 8 Upland 
Road in the R10 zoning district. 
 
Bill Nolan (Savoie Nolan) addressed the Board on behalf of the applicant and stated the lot is 
11,205 sq. ft. and it contains an existing 1-story single family ranch built in 1983.  The applicant 
seeks to construct a new open air 2-car carport with a covered entry into the house. The covered 
portion can be done by right because it is within the setbacks, but the 20’ set back is required and 
they are asking 12.8’ they are asking for 7.2’ of relief for the carport.  The existing wood ramp is 
also within the setback. According to Mr. Nolan, the house is almost conforming in every way.   
 
Mr. Nolan stated that this is the applicant’s retirement home, they are looking to age in place. 
They are looking to park their car and be able to get in and out of their home while out of the 
elements.  According to Mr. Nolan, it would be very difficult to have an enclosed garage in this 
space, and the property will still be conforming on the right side setback.  It is well below the 
height requirement.  
 
Mr. Nolan stated that the very narrow lot creates a hardship.  He stated that the applicant’s lot is a 
good size lot but its narrow and deep and a lot of it is unusable, there is a slope in the rear of the 
property. 
 
Mr. Farinella asked if this location is where they currently park their cars and Mr. Nolan 
confirmed.   
 
Mr. Cosmas stated it is certainly a tough lot, and the neighborhood is full of them. 
 
Sharon Marescalchi, 12 Upland Road, stated she is a direct neighbor on the side of the proposed 
carport.  They did speak with the applicants and went through some of the proposed plans. Ms. 
Marescalchi stated that she and her husband are not for or against the application, they are really 
here on a fact-finding mission. They are concerned whether the car port will ever be enclosed in 
the future.  Additionally, she noted that the street is a little higher than what is shown as the grade 
in the pictures and she is concerned about run off onto their property.   
 
Mr. Butler stated the applicant would need to come back before the Zoning Board if he ever 
wanted to enclose the carport.  
 
Mr. Nolan stated they will marry the carport in with the grade of the driveway.  He added that 
they do have the opportunity to create gutters on this carport to control the water.  
 
MOTION: Mr. Roy moved to close the public hearing. 
Mr. Barone seconded the Motion.
Page 9 of 10 
V otes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy) 
Motion carries. 
 
Mr. Barone commended the applicant for putting this application forward as a carport and not 
trying to put a garage there.  It’s a tricky lot, it’s a very thoughtful application.  Mr. Cosmas 
agreed. 
 
MOTION: Mr. Farinella moved to GRANT a Variance at 8 Upland Road to construct a 
two-car open-air carport within the required 20 ft. front yard setback, seeking 7.2 ft. of 
relief per section 300-34-D3 with the condition that there will be gutters to divert the 
water down and around to the rear of the house and on the basis that the special 
conditions and shape of the lot create a hardship, subject to the plans submitted.    
Mr. Barone seconded the Motion. 
V otes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy) 
Motion carries. 
 
CONTINUED PUBLIC HEARINGS 
 
Jason Irving/21 Bridge Street LLC 
request a Variance to subdivide the lot, retain the existing single-family home and subdivide the 
existing lot to create a new second lot for the construction of an additional single-family home.  
The addition of another single-family home to the lot would be consistent with the general 
character and other lot sizes in the neighborhood.  The property is located at 21 Bridge Street in 
the R10 zoning district.    
 
The applicant submitted a written request to continue the application at 21 Bridge Street to the 
April 22, 2026 meeting of the Board of Appeals, along with the required waiver and agreement. 
 
MOTION:  Ms. Meisenhelter moved to accept and GRANT the request to continue the 
application at 21 Bridge Street to the April 22, 2026 meeting, subject to signing the 
Waiver and Agreement.  Mr. Roy seconded the Motion. 
V otes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy) 
Motion carries. 
 
OTHER BUSINESS 
 
A. Approval of February 25, 2026 Meeting Minutes (Cosmas)   
  
MOTION: Ms. Meisenhelter moved to approve the ZBA Meeting Minutes from 
February 25, 2026, as written.  Mr. Roy seconded the Motion. 
V otes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy) 
Motion carries.
Page 10 of 10 
MOTION:  Mr. Cosmas moved to adjourn the meeting at 9:10pm. 
Ms. Meisenhelter seconded the Motion. 
V otes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy) 
Motion carries. 
 
Leanna Harris, Administrative Assistant 
            Board of Appeals of the Zoning Ordinance
